head: 87480eb410acc467efb835c7abde502432f166ab
summary: SL-063 fixed the bug where a Done top-level row kept its bare name even after an in-place hardlink correction changed its bytes post-settlement. The shipped fix latches a Revised bit from figures captured when a row's pending count reaches zero (not from the Moved call site, per the accepted M2 rework), and TopLevelRowText appends "(revised)" only for that case. All 10 acceptance criteria passed on real data (C:\\Windows and C:\\ProgramData) and in the shipped exe, but two minor code-review findings from a second review pass (file-row test coverage, an XAML-twin fitness rule) remain open and undischarged.

candidates.title: Add the missing real-tree Fact for the file-row settle branch (root-level stale hardlink file, per O-018)
candidates.why: Code review's second pass found Seed's file/link settle capture (introduced by the M2 fix) has no positive test; every existing Revised fact builds folder rows only. Behaviour is correct today (verified by hand with a scratch console) but nothing guards it, and C:\Windows' own root files are hardlinks.

candidates.title: Add the XAML twin fitness rule for the Revised reader (per O-019, matching the repo's SL-044 precedent)
candidates.why: The App-side rule only globs *.cs, so a DataTrigger binding to {Binding Revised} in MainWindow.xaml would pass Fitness untouched -- confirmed by planting exactly that binding, which passed while the .cs plant was caught. The project's fitness.yaml already pairs C# rules with XAML twins elsewhere (SL-044 review m6); this rule has none.

candidates.title: Person decision: should folder-tree drill-down nodes also carry a revision mark?
candidates.why: A Completed scan replaces the top-level list with the folder tree, so today the (revised) mark is visible only mid-scan or after a Cancel -- on real C:\ProgramData it was on screen for about 200ms before the tree replaced it. The design scoped the fix to the top-level list only and left this open; validate confirmed the practical effect (the mark is almost never seen after a normal finish).

candidates.title: Decide whether the scanning header's 'still growing' wording should also cover Done rows whose on-disk bytes are cut short by a Cancel during the probe pass
candidates.why: Validate measured a cancelled run's on-disk total about 748MB below the completed run's, entirely from unprobed Done rows, yet the header only warns about not-read or stopped-partway rows. This is a second, unmarked case of Done implying more finality than the data holds -- the same class of bug as SL-063 itself, in a different place.

candidates.title: Give window-level proof of the (revised) mark without a scratch hook: aggregate revised-row count in --report schema plus an FsaWindowHook mode before EndingShown
candidates.why: No committed window case checks the mark today; validate's only window-level evidence came from a scratch in-process startup hook that was deleted afterwards. The design itself named this as the smallest next step once report-captures-mid-scan-done-row's blockers (hook mode, schema field) are addressed.

candidates.title: Run a full C:\ scan through the shipped exe to confirm the ProgramData row reads (revised) in practice end-to-end
candidates.why: Validate predicted this from ProgramData's stable 16k container-layer corrections but explicitly did not measure it (about 7 minutes of machine time), leaving the shipped-app end-to-end case unconfirmed at full-drive scale.

learned.lesson: TopLevelTracker is single-threaded by construction (owned by the scanner's own thread, enforced by _owner.Check(), no lock anywhere) and Scanner.Execute's SizeFiles -- the only caller of Correct/Credit/Moved -- runs after the listing loop has already emptied _pending. So 'does a correction land after a row settles' is a structural fact provable by reading Scanner.cs:134-166, not something that needs a timing spike or a lock-discipline argument.
learned.evidence: critique's M1 and M4 both guessed at races or unproven ordering; both were overridden by build/code-review simply citing Scanner.cs:152-165 and TopLevelTracker.cs:13-14, which settled them outright.

learned.lesson: TopLevelRow's constructor is internal with exactly one caller, TopLevelTracker.Build -- there is no second construction site to forget a new field on. Concerns about init-only vs positional fields for row properties are usually moot in this type.
learned.evidence: critique's m1 worried a second construction site could silently miss Revised=true; code-review round 1 traced it to a single caller (TopLevelTracker.cs:189) and the finding was overridden.

learned.lesson: This repo's fitness.yaml has an established convention: a C#-only glob rule that guards reads/writes of a field needs a matching XAML-glob twin rule (precedent at fitness.yaml:541-557 and :105-106, from SL-044 review m6). A critique of any new App-side fitness rule should check for this twin explicitly, since it is cheap to check and was missed once already.
learned.evidence: the SL-063 critique reviewed the App-side Revised-reader rule (M3/m2/m3) without raising the missing XAML twin; code-review's second round found it only by planting a DataTrigger binding and citing the existing repo precedent (R2-m2, filed as O-019, still open).

learned.lesson: Code review's second pass can surface fixable gaps (test coverage, rule scope) after build-slice's own pass is already recorded, and this loop did not send the slice back through build-slice to discharge them -- it went straight to validate instead, leaving O-018 and O-019 open at reflect.
learned.evidence: m1 and R2-m2 were both found in code-review round 2, both decided accepted-pending, and both are still listed as owed to build-slice with no further build-slice run recorded.

learned.lesson: On this dev machine, real post-Done corrections are common and recurring on C:\ProgramData (16,309 then 16,305 corrections across two scans, mostly stale container-layer hardlink entries under Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers) but essentially absent on C:\Windows (0/126 across every scan run this slice). Future spikes or validate passes that want to exercise a real positive case for hardlink-driven corrections should target C:\ProgramData, not C:\Windows.
learned.evidence: validate's own C:\Windows run found 0 revised rows (agreeing with the original spike), while its C:\ProgramData run found 5 real revised rows from 16k+ corrections on the first try.

learned.lesson: A Completed scan replaces the top-level list with the folder tree in this app, so any per-row mark added only to top-level rows is visible to a person only while the scan is running or briefly after a Cancel -- never after a normal finish on anything but a very small tree.
learned.evidence: validate measured the (revised) mark on real ProgramData data was drawn for about 200ms before the tree replaced it; the repro tree (23ms total) never shows it on screen at all.

missed.what: When M2 was accepted (moving the settled-capture to two sites: FolderExited for folders and Seed for file/link rows), nobody checked whether test coverage was specified for both new capture sites. The Seed/file-row branch shipped with zero tests and was only caught by code-review's own second round.

The critique reviewed the App-side 'only the row converter reads Revised' fitness rule (raising M3, m2, m3) but did not check it against the project's own established convention that a C#-only glob rule needs a matching XAML-glob twin, even though that convention is already codified in this repo's fitness.yaml with a citation to a prior slice's review finding.
missed.caught_by: code-review (round 2, finding R2-m2 / O-019, confirmed by planting a working DataTrigger binding that passed Fitness untouched)

payload.estimate_error: Sized medium/medium-risk with 1 designer by a person, which fit the actual code change (five files, one bool, one converter case) but undercounted the verification cost: proving the fix on real data required a published self-contained exe, an in-process startup hook, multiple full real-drive scans (C:\\Windows, C:\\ProgramData, a declined full C:\\), and validate's first attempt was cut off mid-run by a provider session limit and had to restart. The risk tier was right for the code; it was light for the real-world proof this bug (a rare, drive-scale timing effect) actually demanded.
payload.reason: Reflection is a summary/analysis stage with no further gate to run; nothing here is blocked pending another stage's output.
payload.summary: SL-063 fixed the bug where a Done top-level row kept its bare name even after an in-place hardlink correction changed its bytes post-settlement. The shipped fix latches a Revised bit from figures captured when a row's pending count reaches zero (not from the Moved call site, per the accepted M2 rework), and TopLevelRowText appends "(revised)" only for that case. All 10 acceptance criteria passed on real data (C:\\Windows and C:\\ProgramData) and in the shipped exe, but two minor code-review findings from a second review pass (file-row test coverage, an XAML-twin fitness rule) remain open and undischarged.
unknowns: Should the revision mark extend to folder-tree drill-down nodes, given a normal Completed finish replaces the top-level list with the tree and the mark is then almost never seen?
Should the scanning header's 'still growing' wording be extended to cover Done rows whose on-disk bytes are left short by a Cancel during the probe pass (measured at ~748MB short in one run)?
Should Unreadable top-level rows, whose partial listing can also be probe-corrected, carry the same revision mark as Done rows?
Why do C:\ProgramData's container-layer hardlink entries stay stale across repeated real scans, when the build's own test tree was refreshed by a single probe pass?
what_went_wrong: Every major gate before validate ran twice: build-check, risk-spike, design-slice, critique and code-review each halted once and were pushed through on a second pass -- mostly by governance decisions to proceed despite an open finding rather than by fixing the finding first.
validate-slice's first attempt was not a content failure but a provider session-limit cutoff, requiring a full second validate pass to get real evidence.

Code-review's second round found two new, fixable gaps (O-018: no test for the file-row settle branch; O-019: missing XAML-twin fitness rule) after build-slice's pass had already been recorded, and the loop proceeded straight to validate rather than sending the slice back through build-slice to close them -- both remain open at reflect.

The critique missed that the project's own fitness.yaml already establishes a C#-rule/XAML-twin convention (from a prior slice's review), so the App-side Revised-reader rule shipped without its twin and had to be caught by a second-round plant in code-review.
